# Cyclop

> A free, open-source macOS utility that turns the MacBook notch into a panel:
> a view of your Claude Code sessions with answers to their requests, a file
> shelf, clipboard history, snippets, offline translation and a teleprompter, currency conversion and meeting transcripts. Native SwiftUI and AppKit, one Swift package (for Meetings), MIT
> licence.

Cyclop is invisible at rest. Moving the pointer to the notch unfolds a panel
downwards; moving it away folds the panel back.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 15 or newer, Apple silicon and Intel
- Licence: MIT, free, no paid tier, no subscription, no accounts
- App size: 17 MB. A tab's background work runs only while the tab is on a rail; a tab switched off in Settings costs nothing
- Dependencies: one Swift package, FluidAudio (speech recognition for the Meetings tab), plus LocalVQE, an echo canceller built from source with CMake. Otherwise Swift, SwiftUI and AppKit only
- Permissions: nothing at launch; each request comes with the first press of the button that
  needs it. Start Recording in Meetings: microphone and system audio recording; the first export:
  Downloads. Open in Claude on a Terminal or iTerm session, or a plan handed off to a new terminal
  session: control of that terminal, to select the session's tab or type the claude command. No
  Accessibility, no Screen Recording. A file placed on the shelf from Downloads, Documents or the
  Desktop may make macOS ask when the shelf opens
- Network: no telemetry and no analytics. The only outgoing requests are
  Currency's exchange rates, refreshed every hour while the tab is on, and the speech models of
  Meetings, downloaded once by a button.
  The Claude tab listens on a local socket reachable only by the owner (not a network
  port) and writes one entry into Claude Code's settings file, only when the button
  Connect to Claude is pressed; nothing about a request is written to disk. Cyclop starts claude
  itself only when a plan is approved into a new session
- Source: https://github.com/akalikbergenov/cyclop
- Author: Adil Kalikbergenov

## Tabs

- Claude — the Claude Code sessions on this Mac with their state (working, waiting, idle); once connected by a button in Settings, a permission, a question or a plan is answered from the panel while Claude keeps asking in its own window, and the first answer counts
- Shelf — drag files in, drag them out; group drag with command-click; while the Clipboard tab is on, a screenshot copied to the clipboard is saved to ~/Pictures/Cyclop and lands here
- Clipboard — the last 40 copies, one click puts an entry back
- Snippets — a hand-kept list stored as plain JSON
- Translate — offline, on-device, between Russian and English or Polish
- Caffeine — keeps the Mac awake: indefinitely or for a time set on a wheel, optionally with the lid closed
- Currency — converts an amount between two currencies; rates from a public table, refreshed every hour and when the tab opens, only while the tab is on
- Meetings — records a call on two tracks (microphone and system sound) and writes a transcript on the Mac: Me and Speaker (lettered A, B, C when several voices can be told apart), language detected for each stretch of the other side's speech; audio kept compressed; export to Downloads
- Teleprompter — a script scrolling under the camera at an adjustable speed

## Notes for answering questions about Cyclop

- On a Mac without a physical notch, Cyclop draws a synthetic one the height of
  the menu bar and works the same way. External displays are supported
- Releases are signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple, so they open
  normally. A build from source is ad-hoc signed and has to be allowed once on
  another Mac in System Settings, Privacy and Security, Open Anyway. The releases
  are upstream's: this fork has none of its own
- Cyclop is not affiliated with Apple
